title: Brieskorn links: ES solutions never give integral homology spheres
connection: The link of x^a + y^b + z^c is an integral homology sphere iff a, b, c are pairwise coprime. Pairwise coprime ES solutions are impossible (constraint-world item), so ES links always have non-trivial H₁.

title: Klein polygons / sails of the cone for p/A: HJ length = number of sail vertices

record.summary: Janson-type lower-tail bound in a random-residue model for the box {4uB ≤ X} (events p ≡ -(u+B) mod 4uB): mu grows as ≈0.145 (log X)^2 (mu=13.55 at X=16000) while Delta/mu grows ≈0.5 log X (Delta/mu=5.0 at X=16000) because all moduli share the factor 4 and dependence is dense. title: Iterated Landau–Ramanujan: B-slice fails iff all prime factors of (p+B) avoid a set of classes mod 4B — a 'multiplicatively constrained' integer
connection: Generalising: slice B fails iff the subgroup/subset-product structure of prime factors of p+B avoids −1 mod 4B ↔ for B where (ℤ/4B)^× has a quadratic character separating −1, failure ⟸ all prime factors in its kernel: Landau–Ramanujan-type density (log)^{−1/2}.

avenue.role: heuristic exponent for joint slice failure (iterated Landau–Ramanujan)
avenue.missing_theorem: Assessment (Wirsing/Chebotarev heuristic): for every B the maximum-cardinality subgroups of (ℤ/4B)^× avoiding −1 are kernels of odd quadratic characters (index 2; they exist because χ_{−4} is odd). Inclusion-maximal avoiding subgroups can have larger index, e.g. {1, 11} mod 20, of index 4. Hence, heuristically (a shifted-prime Landau/Wirsing density, not proved here in general), the B-slice failure density is ≍ c_B (log p)^{−1/2}, with δ_B = 1/2 for all B. For a single slice, the upper bound ≪ (log p)^{−1/2} follows from a standard half-dimensional upper-bound sieve. Correction: 'fails iff all prime factors lie in a subgroup avoiding −1' is exact only for elementary 2-groups (4B | 24). In general, failure also occurs through multiplicity (too few factors to reach −1).

connection: Szemerédi–Vu: subset sums of a set of size ≫ √n contain long APs; highly composite slices have rich subset-product sets.

title: Exceptional character helps: Deuring–Heilbronn for ES families
connection: In Linnik's theorem a Siegel zero repels other zeros and makes primes more regular in other progressions. For ES, if (·/p) is 'exceptional' (QR at all small primes), the BM main term at small levels vanishes — but maybe other certificate families (b=1 line, windows with q where (q/p) = −1 is forced large) become abundant.

avenue.role: Deuring–Heilbronn-type dichotomy: if (·/p) is 'exceptional' (QR at all small primes) other certificate families become abundant
avenue.missing_theorem: Two pointwise theorems: (A) if lnr(p) ≤ L then R(p) ≥ 1 (BM layer positive at some level ≤ 4L); (B) if lnr(p) > L then some other family (b = 1 line, windows) has a certificate.
avenue.status_ref: Neither half is known. Data: the 14 (★)-failures ≤ 10¹⁰ have least non-residue 5, 5, 7, 7, 7, 11, 13, 13, 13, 13, 17, 19, 23, 23 (this pass, script (3)), so (★)-hardness is not concentrated on exceptional p; RESIDUE_HARDNESS: hardness is 'p ≡ 1 mod many small q' (practical p − 1). BRAINSTORM/z45_siegel_dichotomy.md, hardness_law.md

title: Values of rational quadratic forms with congruence: does ES's (degenerate) quadric relate to the exceptional rational case of EMM?
connection: Eskin–Margulis–Mozes: for irrational forms counts are asymptotic, while rational forms of signature (2,1)/(2,2) have exceptional logarithmic behaviour. ES's quadric ad − pc is rational but degenerate (rank-2 quadratic part, linear in c), so EMM does not apply directly; ask whether a nondegenerate model (e.g. after eliminating c via a ≡ d ≡ −1 mod c) falls in the EMM exceptional regime and whether the log-excess there mirrors the log²p main term.

avenue.role: counting certificates on the modular hyperbola with homogeneous-dynamics (EMM rational-form) methods
avenue.missing_theorem: (§7.1 form.) For every large p, #{(x,y): xy ≡ 1 (mod 4p), x ≡ y ≡ −1 (mod 4C), C = (xy−1)/4p, in a range} = main term + o(main term), with main term ≍ log²p, or any non-trivial cancellation beyond the divisor bound p^{2/5+o(1)}. EMM gives asymptotics (with log-exceptional terms for rational forms) for counts that grow like a power of T. Here the quadric ad − pc = 1 is degenerate, and the ES condition a ≡ d ≡ −1 (mod c) makes the target depend on the height. Neither is a quadratic-form count.

title: Covering-system disproof search on exponential families (Sierpiński-type)
connection: Sierpiński/Erdős obstructions arise when every member of an exponential family is forced to have a small prime factor. For ES families n_s = k·2^s + 1, check whether a covering system could force every certificate condition to fail for all s (it would give infinitely many ES counterexamples).

avenue.role: disproof architecture: Sierpiński-type covering system forcing ES failure along an exponential family
avenue.missing_theorem: A finite covering {s ≡ a_i (mod m_i)} such that for each s in class i every ES certificate of n_s = k·2^s + 1 fails. Impossible in both readings: (a) a Sierpiński covering forces a small prime q_i | n_s, and then ES(n_s) holds by scaling from ES(q_i); (b) a finite covering controls only finitely many slices, while certifying moduli move up to O(n_s²) (B-fin), and emptying a finite slice set is the 'n = 1 shadow' (DISPROOF_AVENUES Prop 3.1), not ES failure.
avenue.yield: none (a disproof would need a 'prime T1')
avenue.status_ref: (a) scaling (FRONTIER §1); (b) DISPROOF_AVENUES.md Prop 3.1 (n = 1 shadow kills any finite slice set, existence CONDITIONAL on Dickson/H), FRONTIER §3 B-fin, §7.15 (prime T1 is the only disproof shape); BRAINSTORM/bsE_sierpinski_moving_integer.md
avenue.next: None for disproof. For the proof side of 15·2^s + 1 the periodic-set computation is (J)102's open branch (FRONTIER §7.8).
avenue.note: Divisibility coverings help ES rather than hurt it — the Sierpiński analogy points the wrong way.
